counterexample_text: Define h:[0,1]→R by h(0)=0 and h(x)=1 for every x in (0,1]. Then h is differentiable on (0,1) with h'(u)=0≤0 for all u in (0,1), but for any u in (0,1), h(u)=1>0=h(0).
statement_fingerprint: Let h : [0,1] -> R be differentiable on (0,1). If h'(u) <= 0 for every u in (0,1), then h(u) <= h(0) for every u with 0 <= u < 1.::{"domain_restrictions": ["h is defined on the closed interval [0,1].", "differentiability of h is assumed only on the open interval (0,1).", "the condition h'(u) <= 0 is required for all u strictly between 0 and 1.", "the conclusion is required for all u in the half-open interval [0,1)."], "normalized_claim": "If h is differentiable on (0,1) and maps [0,1] to real numbers, and if for all u in (0,1) the derivative satisfies h'(u) is less than or equal to 0, then for all u in [0,1) the value h(u) is less than or equal to h(0).", "quantifier_order": ["There exists a function h mapping [0,1] to real numbers, differentiable on (0,1).", "For every real u with u in (0,1), assume h'(u) <= 0.", "For every real u with 0 <= u < 1, conclude h(u) <= h(0)."], "variables": [{"domain": "all real x in the interval [0,1]", "name": "h", "role": "subject function; differentiable on the open interval (0,1)", "type": "function from real numbers to real numbers"}, {"domain": "open interval (0,1) when used in the derivative hypothesis; domain [0,1) when used in the conclusion", "name": "u", "role": "point where the derivative inequality is evaluated; point where the function value comparison is asserted", "type": "real number"}], "witness_dependencies": []}
summary: The lemma is false as stated. The hypothesis only assumes differentiability on the open interval (0,1), so it gives no control over the endpoint value h(0). A function can have h'(u) <= 0 on (0,1) and still satisfy h(u) > h(0) for some u in [0,1), so the claimed conclusion fails.
